'''Jean-Pierre Tignol''' (b. 1954) is a Belgian mathematician and historian of mathematics specializing in the field of [[Quadratic form|quadratic forms]] and [[Linear algebraic group|linear algebraic groups]].<ref name=kons>[https://www.uni-konstanz.de/zukunftskolleg/news/current-news/single-news/senior-fellowship-for-jean-pierre-tignol/ Senior Fellowship for Jean-Pierre Tignol] University of Konstanz, April 9, 2010</ref>  He is a full professor emeritus at [[Université catholique de Louvain]].<ref name=tits>[https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202301/noti2601/noti2601.html?adat=January%202023&trk=2601&galt=none&cat=interest&pdfissue=202301&pdffile=rnoti-p77.pdf Tributes to Jacques Tits: Jean-Pierre Tignol], Notices of the [[American Mathematical Society]]</ref>

==Education and career==
Tignol was awarded a PhD (1988) at the Université catholique de Louvain for his thesis ''Involution bodies of finite rank at their center and with characteristic other than 21'' written under the supervision of [[Jacques Tits]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=22812 Jean-Pierre Tignol] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref> He subsequently became a professor at the same university.<ref name=tits/> He is the author of numerous papers on algebra and is responsible for extending concepts and results from quadratic form theory to the study of [[*-algebra|involution algebras]].<ref name=kons/> In 1996, he was invited by the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in [[Budapest]] to speak on "Algebras with involution and classical groups".<ref name=ecom>[https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/european-congress-of-mathematics-antal-balog/1115590271 European Congress of Mathematics: Budapest, July 22-26, 1996] Barnes & Noble, Inc.</ref>

In his 2001 book, ''Galois' Theory of Algebraic Equations'', he explored the evolution of algebra from ancient [[Babylon]] to the eras of [[Évariste Galois|Galois]] and [[Alexander Grothendieck|Grothendieck]]. A review by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] said, "Anybody with an interest in algebra or the history of mathematics should look at this book. And of course it goes without saying that it belongs in any good university library."<ref name=hist>[https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/galois-theory-of-algebraic-equations Galois' Theory of Algebraic Equations: Reviewed by Mark Hunacek], 02/21/2016, Mathematical Association of America</ref>

==Books==
* 2001 ''[https://openlibrary.org/works/OL22321543W/Galois%27_theory_of_algebraic_equations?edition= Galois' Theory of Algebraic Equations]'' World Scientific, {{ISBN|9789814704694}}<ref name=hist/>
* 1998 ''[https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/involutions The Book of Involutions]'' (with [[Max-Albert Knus]], [[Alexander Merkurjev]] and [[Markus Rost]]), American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI [PDF]<ref>''[https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/involutions The Book of Involutions]'' (with Markus Rost, et.al.), Colloquium Publications 44, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI</ref>

* 2015 ''[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-16360-4 Value Functions on Simple Algebras, and Associated Graded Rings]'' (with AR Wadsworth) Springer Cham, {{ISBN|978-3-319-16359-8}}

==Papers==
* 1993 "On the signature of an involution", (with [[David W. Lewis (mathematician)|David W. Lewis]]), Arch. Math. (Basel) 60, no. 2, 128–135.
* 1979 "Division algebras of degree 4 and 8 with involution", (with [[Shimshon Amitsur]] and L. H. Rowen), Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 115, p. 691-693
* 1987 [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1987-302-01/S0002-9947-1987-0887507-6/?active=current "Totally ramified valuations on finite-dimensional division algebras"], (with A. R. Wadsworth), [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 302, p. 223-250
* 1995 "The multipliers of similitudes and the Brauer group of homogeneous varieties", (with [[Alexander Merkurjev]]), Journal fur die Reine und Angewandte Mathematik, vol. 461, p. 13-48
* 1993 "Hyperbolic involutions", (with [[Eva Bayer-Fluckiger]] and D. B. Shapiro), Mathematische Zeitschrift, vol. 214, p. 461-476

==Awards==
In 1994 he was awarded the [[Eugene Catalan Prize]] by the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in Belgium.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Recognizing Excellence in the Mathematical Sciences : an international compilation of awards, prizes, and recipients|date=1997|publisher=[[JAI Press]]|author=Jaguszewski, Janice M.|isbn=0762302356|location=Greenwich, Conn.|oclc=37513025}}</ref>

In the years 2010 to 2012, Jean-Pierre Tignol was awarded several Senior Fellowships of the Zukunftskolleg at the [[University of Konstanz]].<ref>[https://www.uni-konstanz.de/zukunftskolleg/community/senior-fellows/ Senior fellows of Zukunftskolleg] from [[University of Konstanz]]</ref>
